headline: Nvidia is falling on a CEO investigation while every other chip stock rises, and big news lands in 7 days, so buying the dip today is a gamble, not a plan.

messages.text: I'd skip this one. Nvidia is down about 4.5% today, and it is the only big chip stock falling while the rest of the group is rising.

The reason is not a normal market wobble. Nvidia's own board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over his ties to an executive at a company that is being looked at for chip smuggling. Nobody knows yet how far this goes.
The charts all point down. The price is below its short and long average lines on every timeframe. Buying now is like trying to catch a falling knife.
Bull will say 'it's oversold, a bounce is due'. Oversold means it fell very fast. But a stock can stay oversold for a long time when the bad news is still unfolding.

More trouble is lined up. Congress is pushing chip limits, Huang may be called to a closed-door briefing on Nov 18, and Nvidia reports earnings on Nov 17. That is 7 days away, so a quick day trade could get caught in headline swings.
There is also a shareholder lawsuit reported after the close. Lawyers and headlines can hit the price again at any moment, and a short-term trade has little room to wait it out.

argument:
The trade is a long on NVDA at $170.64, down 4.49% from yesterday's $178.67 close. The drop is news driven, not a routine pullback: NVDA was the only chip stock down on Monday while the PHLX semiconductor index rose over 6.8% (per a Yahoo Finance report), so this is stock-specific key-person and governance risk, not sector weakness that can reverse with the sector. The board opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over his ties to a Megaspeed executive; Bloomberg reported Nvidia's general counsel contacted a Commerce official about a smuggling probe involving Megaspeed; a shareholder lawsuit reportedly followed the close.

Technically every timeframe is bearish: EMA9 below EMA21, price below SMA50 and SMA200 on 5m, 15m and 1h. RSI14 is 25.1 (5m), 28.5 (15m) and 27.6 (1h). Oversold readings in a news-driven downtrend are not buy signals; they show momentum, and the 1h MACD histogram is still falling (-0.47 versus -0.35 before). Price is also below the session VWAP of 171.75, so the average buyer today is underwater. The 1h SMA200 is 216.31, far above, and the 1h window fell 22.6%. The 52-week low is $164.27, only about 3.7% below, so there is little cushion before a new low.

Risk events: the guard shows CLEAR for scheduled macro events today, but NVDA earnings are about 7 days away (Nov 17 per 247WallSt) and Huang may face a House briefing Nov 18, with possible subpoena. NDAA chip-export provisions are being debated. Headlines can arrive at any time and an intraday stop can gap through. With the 1h ATR at 3.86, a normal hourly move is about 2.3% of the price, so tight stops get hit by noise.

evidence.claim: NVDA $170.64, -4.49% on the day, below VWAP 171.75; RSI14 25.1 (5m), 28.5 (15m), 27.6 (1h); below SMA50 and SMA200 on all three timeframes
evidence.plain: Nvidia is falling hard today and sits below all its key average lines. Low RSI shows it fell fast, not that it has stopped.

evidence.claim: Nvidia board opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over ties to a Megaspeed executive; shareholder suit reportedly followed the close; Bloomberg says Nvidia's general counsel contacted a Commerce official about a Megaspeed smuggling probe
evidence.plain: The company's own board is investigating its CEO, and the full story is not known yet.

evidence.claim: NVDA was the only chip stock in the red Monday; AMD +~4%, Broadcom +~3%, PHLX Semiconductor Index +6.8%
evidence.plain: Other chip makers went up while Nvidia went down, so this is Nvidia's own problem, not the whole sector.

evidence.claim: Congress weighing China AI-chip limits in NDAA (AI Overwatch Act, Chip Security Act); Nvidia earnings Nov 17; closed-door briefing requested for Nov 18, possible subpoena; stock down 22.07% over the past month
evidence.plain: More political and earnings news is coming within a week, and the stock already dropped about a fifth in a month.
evidence.value: Earnings Nov 17; briefing Nov 18; -22.07% in 1 month

evidence.claim: Three House chairs asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on Nov 18 about his contacts with a former Megaspeed executive and espionage safeguards
evidence.plain: Congress wants Huang to explain himself in person, which keeps the story in the headlines.
evidence.source: Web search summary (TheNextWeb / LetsDataScience, snippet only)

evidence.claim: Polymarket odds Huang announces resignation or is removed by Dec 31, 2026: 18%
evidence.plain: Traders on a betting site think there is about a 1 in 5 chance the CEO leaves this year, which shows how uncertain things are.
A normal one-hour move is about $3.86, so a tight stop gets hit by noise, the yearly low is not far below, and selling pressure was still growing on the hourly chart.

plan_flaws: No plan numbers yet; any stop tighter than about 1x the 1h ATR ($3.86) sits inside a normal hourly swing
Oversold RSI (25 to 28) is being used as a buy signal while trend, MACD and VWAP all point down
Headline risk (board probe, lawsuit, NDAA, Nov 18 briefing, Nov 17 earnings) is not covered by the event guard, which shows CLEAR only for scheduled macro data
The nearest known floor, the 52-week low of $164.27, is only about $6.37 below the price, so a break would leave no support
plan_flaws_plain: A safety exit placed too close would be triggered by normal wiggles of about $3.86 per hour.
'Oversold' only means it fell fast. Nothing on the charts says the falling has stopped.
The calendar says CLEAR, but the real danger is surprise news about the CEO, which no calendar shows.
If the yearly low at $164.27 breaks, there is no obvious floor nearby.
conditions_to_reconsider: Only after the board investigation gives a clear result or the stock reclaims the session VWAP (about $171.75) and holds it for an hour on rising volume, with the other chip stocks still strong. Better yet, wait until after the Nov 17 earnings report.
